messages.content: Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.

message.content: No. Pointwise convergence implies uniform convergence only under additional constraints, such as monotonicity or bounded derivatives. Consider Weierstrass-like examples where oscillations grow near endpoints. Polynomials can approximate discontinuous limits pointwise yet fail uniform bounds. Uniform continuity requires equicontinuity, absent here. Thus, pointwise alone insufficient for uniform guarantee.
